steps.say: Fiction is made up. Non-fiction gives true information about the real world.
Each fiction genre has features. A mystery has clues. Fantasy has magic. Science fiction looks to the future.
Playscripts show who speaks. Stage directions in brackets tell actors what to do.
steps.show: MAYA: (opening the door) Is anyone there?

steps.say: Non-fiction texts have a purpose. A recount tells what happened. Instructions tell how to do something. A report gives facts.
A balanced argument gives more than one side before it reaches a view.

check.prompt: Which text type is written to tell the reader how to do something?

options.why: A report gives facts about a topic.
A fable is a made-up story with a lesson.

hints: Think about the purpose of the text.
Look for the one that gives commands.
It uses steps, such as first, next and then.
check.explanation: Instructions tell the reader what to do, step by step.
